exposure: Mode of delivery (Vacuum-assisted delivery, Second-stage caesarean delivery, Spontaneous vaginal delivery)
cohort: 253 children born by low-station or mid-station vacuum-assisted delivery, 247 children born after spontaneous vaginal delivery, and 86 children born via second-stage caesarean delivery
finding: Children born after vacuum-assisted delivery or second-stage caesarean delivery exhibited an increased rate of long-term neurodevelopmental difficulties in motor skills and perception compared with spontaneous vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: Children born after vacuum-assisted delivery or second-stage caesarean delivery exhibited an increased rate of long-term neurodevelopmental difficulties in motor skills and perception compared with spontaneous vaginal delivery.
